fatal_errors: The proposed method is computational prediction, not the liquid-metal dealloying fabrication method used to produce the large-scale RHEA-Cu composite.
It omits immersion of directionally segregated WTaVTi in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h.
It provides no account of selective Ti-Cu exchange, retention of W/Ta/V-rich ligaments, or formation of the W-rich passivating interlayer that stabilizes the interface.
No cited evidence supports the claim that ab initio calculations themselves enable the stated large-scale reaction or stable microstructure.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the general RHEA-Cu compatibility problem and invokes high-temperature thermodynamics, but it does not reconstruct the relevant experimental solution. The target method is liquid-metal dealloying, in which Cu selectively replaces Ti/V-rich interdendritic regions while a W-rich interlayer arrests further reaction and stabilizes a directionally aligned bicontinuous composite. Ab initio calculations could potentially guide alloy design, but they are not a fabrication process and do not explain the observed millimeter-scale reaction or interfacial stability. The proposed validation is also underspecified because neither the comparison process nor quantitative stability criteria are defined.
